title: Room booking lifecycle
idea: The room booking lifecycle is a state machine: a Booking starts BOOKED and may move only through allowed transitions to CHECKED_IN, COMPLETED, CANCELLED or RELEASED.
points: BOOKED becomes CHECKED_IN, CANCELLED, or RELEASED when nobody checks in.
CHECKED_IN becomes COMPLETED at the end time; three states are final.
Only BOOKED and CHECKED_IN block the room; other states free it.
Every change goes through `moveTo`, so illegal moves are refused in one place.

messages.label: book(4, 10:00-11:00)
messages.note: The organizer asks for a room for four people.

messages.label: isFree, add(BK-1)
messages.note: The service checks the room's Calendar and stores BK-1 as BOOKED.

messages.label: BK-1 BOOKED
messages.note: The organizer gets the booking id and the room name.

messages.label: sweep(10:05)
messages.note: The sweeper runs every minute. At 10:05 BK-1 is still inside its grace period.

messages.label: checkIn(BK-1)
messages.note: The organizer taps check in at the room panel. BK-1 moves BOOKED to CHECKED_IN.

messages.label: sweep(10:12)
messages.note: At 10:12 BK-1 is CHECKED_IN, so the sweeper leaves it alone.

messages.label: sweep(11:00)
messages.note: At the end time the sweeper moves BK-1 to COMPLETED.

messages.label: remove(BK-1)
messages.note: A final state no longer blocks the room. Without a check-in, RELEASED would free it at 10:10.

code.title: Status enum with rules
code.caption: Allowed moves live in the enum. Booking asks the enum before every change.

walk.text: BK-1 checks in, completes, then a late cancel is tried.
BK-2 is released as a no-show; a late check-in is tried.
BK-3 is cancelled early, then we ask whether it still blocks the room.
An `EnumMap` lists the allowed next states for each state.
Refuse and report an illegal move; otherwise record the new state.

pitfalls: Do not set `status` from controllers; route every change through `moveTo`.
A released no-show must not be revived; the room may already be rebooked.
Run the sweeper with an injected clock, so tests can replay any minute.

quiz.q: What does the fifth line of BookingLifecycle print?
quiz.why: RELEASED has no allowed next states. `canMoveTo(CHECKED_IN)` is false, so `moveTo` prints the refusal and keeps RELEASED.

takeaway: Allowed moves live in one enum; everything else is refused.

starters: Should an organizer be able to extend a CHECKED_IN meeting?
Why not delete cancelled bookings instead of keeping a status?
How often should the no-show sweeper run?
